title: Normalized slice evaluation for continuous coefficient inverse image
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For any scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the continuous coefficient sheaves $A_W(V)=C(|V|,A)$, $E_W(V)=C(|V|,E)$ with constant-section normalization [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients, lem-weil-pbc-continuous-ring-functions-sheaf]. For a noetherian finite-dimensional $X$ with $\ell$ invertible these identify with $B_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ and $B_X[1/\varpi]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Let $u:U\to X$ be any object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with no noetherian hypothesis on $U$. Under the localization equivalence $U_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is canonically the slice restriction $F|_U(V\to U)=F(V\to X)$. It sends the continuous integral and rational coefficient rings to $A_U,E_U$, identically on the continuous functions of the same underlying $V$. It preserves every finite constant quotient, its quotient transitions and the coefficient projections. In the inverse-image indexing category $\mathcal I_V$ this identification is induced by the initial object $(V\to X,(s,\mathrm{id}_V))$, where $s:V\to U$ is the structure map; thus it is normalized for the actual inverse-image construction, including its sheafification. Module restriction is exact and its derived functor is termwise restriction [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence]. In particular, for an etale morphism $g:X'\to X$ between schemes with the same hypotheses the finite-quotient structural maps are isomorphisms $g^{-1}B_X\cong B_{X'}$, $g^{-1}E_X\cong E_{X'}$, and $E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}(-)$ is exact ordinary inverse image. The same conclusion holds for a locally closed immersion by the specified immersion coefficient isomorphisms. Site restriction of an ambient derived pullback is the corresponding restricted module pullback; all these identifications preserve coefficient maps and constant sections.
